words: 0.4.2 adds one optional column, market_value_eod_claim (measured or inferred), required on every PRESENT Orion row and null on an ABSENT row; the optional_columns gains that sixth entry and the enums block gains its enum. The 19 columns, their types, schema_hash, the five earlier optional columns and every earlier enum except return_basis are byte-identical; served_day_rules, and the flows, business_date and account_id rules of source_rules are unmoved; rule24_record keeps every earlier key and adds v042. Amendment 2 repairs return_basis: VENDOR_REPORTED leaves its enum (now TWR and NOT_MEASURABLE), source_requires is removed, and a top-level source_provenance maps each source value to who computed it (orion vendor-computed; the two Black Diamond sources Opal-computed); source_rules.orion.return_basis now says Orion rows carry TWR and provenance is read from source. Every earlier NON-Orion writer still validates, with or without the claim. An Orion writer must now carry the claim on a PRESENT row, and an Orion row labelled VENDOR_REPORTED no longer validates; the one Orion writer, the Scope adapter, already writes the claim (surprise row IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W223-S1). The 0.4.0, 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 test files all pass; the 0.4.1 file took a bounded amendment (a claim-aware validator and claim-carrying fixtures, and its superseded return_basis and source_requires assertions re-pointed). NOT PROVEN: that the Scope adapter writes the claim as the contract declares it, that its parquet output validates against this contract, or that any consumer rejects an inferred value.
